stimulus: Proton may be witnessed by a neutron or by outer closure; test whether the obligation belongs to a body or a face.
source_geometry: Actual occupied bodies, marked roles and triangular contacts from saved local-reference constructions; no reinterpretation of an electron as a whole octahedron.
body_hypothesis: Each neutron filler needs at least one occupied proton witness, and each proton body has one witness slot. Other proton bodies may use an exterior boundary face. A neutron may touch several protons; body exclusivity applies to the proton, not the neutron.
face_hypothesis: Each actual P-N contact supplies its proton-face witness; distinct proton faces may be supplied by different neutrons. Every neutron filler must have at least one such occupied-proton contact. Remaining proton faces must connect to the unbounded vacant complement, not an enclosed cavity.
outer_boundary_test: Flood vacant neighboring primitive cells. Reaching any cell with a vertex beyond the occupied coordinate bounds certifies connection to infinity. Exhaustion certifies a bounded cavity. A resource stop remains unknown.
boundary: This is a geometric/support hypothesis test, not a new native admission rule, physical stability law, electron enclosure model, or symmetry derivation.
risk: Compare both hypotheses with already certified H1/H2 and saved heavier constructions; retain any rejected source certificate as counterevidence rather than changing contacts or adding virtual occupied protons.
